solution:
**(A)** Comb jelly

Comb jellies belong to phylum Ctenophora, which the chapter says is represented by very few members and is therefore considered one of the minor phyla. A jelly fish (*Aurelia*) belongs to Cnidaria, while *Herdmania* and *Salpa* are urochordates, a subphylum of the large phylum Chordata.

**(C)** Rohu

Rohu (*Labeo rohita*) is a bony fish. A fish heart is two chambered with single circulation, so it always carries only deoxygenated blood and is called a venous heart. The crocodile has a four chambered heart, and the salamander and the toad are amphibians with three chambered hearts that receive oxygenated blood as well.

**(C)** mesoderm is present in patches

*Ascaris* is a triploblastic pseudocoelomate. Its body cavity is a pseudocoel because the mesoderm does not form a continuous lining; it lies as scattered patches between the ectoderm and the endoderm. A body cavity is therefore present, mesoglea is the non-living layer of diploblastic animals such as cnidarians, and the endoderm lines the gut as a continuous layer.

[Note: the chapter only calls *Ascaris* pseudocoelomate; standard biology gives that a pseudocoelom arises because mesoderm is present as scattered pouches rather than a complete lining.]

**(A)** Presence of teeth

In birds the jaws are without teeth and are modified into a beak, so presence of teeth is the incorrect statement. The chapter states that birds do have scales on their hind limbs, that their RBCs are biconvex and nucleated, and that their bones are hollow (pneumatic) to reduce body weight.

**(C)** Millipede

A millipede is an arthropod, and arthropods have a tough, non-living chitinous exoskeleton that they shed periodically by moulting. *Dentalium* (tusk shell) is a mollusc with a calcareous shell, while *Antedon* (sea lily) and the sea urchin are echinoderms with an endoskeleton of calcareous ossicles.
